intro_md:
Written on 29 September 2026. This records the line pass made outside this repository on 28–29 September, in the conversation summarised in `New - Re-plan/Claude Handoff.md` (§3). The author accepted every change, and the chapter now matches the text they supplied.

The chapter as it stood before the pass is saved unchanged as `Drafts/Chapter 1 - A War Without Sound (Draft 2, before the line pass).md`, and every change here is measured against it. The rounds before the pass are in `Chapter 1 - Changes.md`. **Later rounds go on this list** (`Drafts/Chapter 1 - change list (line pass).json`).

Each reason says where it comes from: the handoff when it gives one, or Claude's reading when it doesn't. Changes tagged as the author's own lines replaced something the author wrote or designed; they are listed below, under "The author's own lines this pass replaced".
summary_md:
## The author's own lines this pass replaced

Changes {tag:authorline}. The handoff records them as accepted. They are listed here because the skill asks that every change to the author's own lines be flagged.

changes.title: He opens his eyes
changes.before: A broad shape leaned over him, blocking the worst of the light.
changes.after: He cracked his eyes open to find a broad shape leaning over him, blocking the worst of the light.
changes.why: This is in the opening, which the author wrote. The handoff, §3: "Alaric explicitly reopens his eyes before perceiving Gerolt's face and movements." Three paragraphs earlier he shuts them against the sun.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: The man glancing at the field
changes.before: The voice was rough, and its owner kept glancing past him at the field even while he waited for an answer, the way a man checks a door he already knows won't stay shut.
changes.after: The voice was rough, and its owner kept glancing past him at the field even while he waited for an answer.
changes.why: This is in the opening, which the author wrote. Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the comparison ("the way a man checks a door he already knows won't stay shut") is one Alaric couldn't make from anything he has lived through on the page. Principle 5.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: The clothes, on the field
changes.before:
No iron plate. No boiled leather. No crest stamped into a breastplate, no weapon at his hip. Only his clothes, and they were wrong somehow—the cloth smooth where the man's own coat was coarse, and fitted to him without a single seam split. Not one tear. Not one puncture anywhere on it, for all the blood soaked into the fabric.

The stitching seemed to trouble the man most. He rolled one seam between two fingers, then another, frowning at stitches too small and even to easily separate. Whatever he was looking for, he didn't find it.
changes.after: No armour. No weapon. Only blood-soaked clothes without a single tear. The man rolled one seam between two fingers, frowned at the tiny, even stitches, and let it go.
changes.why: This is in the opening, which the author wrote. The handoff, §3: "The clothes anomaly was separated into two functions: survival anomaly on the field, identity evidence in the cabin." On the field, what matters is that he has no armour, no weapon and no tear. The cloth and the stitching are left for Gerolt to question in the cabin ("Thirty years of traders on this road and I've never seen stitching like that").
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: Gerolt's back
changes.after: Gerolt's fist fell away from his back.
changes.why: The handoff, §3: "'Gerolt forgot about his back' was replaced with observable physical action." The boy can see the fist leave his back; he can't see Gerolt forget.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: Who made them
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): Gerolt is asking about the clothes, and the boy answers about "them".
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: Gerolt studies him
changes.before: Gerolt read his face and gave up on explaining. He set the mug on the floor and held out one hand between them, palm up.
changes.after: Gerolt studied him for a moment. Then he set the mug on the floor and held out one hand between them, palm up.
changes.why: The handoff, §3: "'Gerolt read his face and gave up on explaining' was removed in favour of what Alaric could actually see."
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: Close enough to touch
changes.before: "I couldn't see their face." The boy caught at Gerolt's sleeve. "They were close enough that they should have reached me, but they kept running and never came any nearer. Their mouth kept moving. They were saying something to me—"
changes.after: "I couldn't see their face." The boy caught at Gerolt's sleeve. "They were close enough to touch me, but they kept running and never came any nearer. Their mouth kept moving. They were saying something to me—"
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): a plainer way of saying the figure was near and still never reached him. The handoff (§3) describes the vision as "a running figure, the open hand and the unreachable distance".
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).
